full_description:
Full-time 40 hours/week

Monday-Friday 8am-4:30pm

Hybrid remote- must be onsite between 6-12 days/month

Summary:

The Data Scientist within the Surgery Research Enterprise at Akron Children's Hospital plays a pivotal role in advancing the department's research and analytics capabilities. Reporting to the Director of Research, the position is integral to the Surgery Research Enterprise and supports clinical research, outcomes research, and advanced analytics across surgical divisions. The Data Scientist is expected to work independently, collaborate with investigators, and develop and lead research and data science projects from concept through analysis and dissemination.

Responsibilities:

1. Supports the development of advanced analytics and data science capabilities within the Surgery Research Enterprise by gathering feedback and guidance from leaders, investigators, stakeholders, and peers. Contributes to implementing a clear roadmap aligned with surgical research priorities.

2. Develops and maintains collaborative relationships with investigators, clinical leaders, research staff, and partners. Builds an understanding of the clinical and research context and the strategic goals of the surgical divisions.

3. Cultivates external partnerships with professional associations, communities, universities, research institutes, government agencies, and solution providers or vendors to advance research and analytics objectives.

4. Collects and explores raw data from multiple sources to identify patterns, trends, and potential insights. Cleans, transforms, and validates data to ensure its quality and suitability for research and analysis.

5. Designs, develops, implements, and optimizes predictive and prescriptive models using statistical techniques and machine learning algorithms to improve accuracy and performance.

6. Identifies and engineers relevant features from datasets to strengthen model predictive power. Collaborates with clinical investigators and domain experts to extract meaningful features that improve model effectiveness.

7. Develops, evaluates, validates, and refines statistical and machine learning models to ensure accuracy, relevance, and effectiveness in clinical and research settings. Applies advanced analytical techniques to support clinically meaningful surgical research.

8. Creates compelling data visualizations and dashboards that communicate insights and findings effectively to technical and non-technical stakeholders using Tableau, Power BI, or custom code.

9. Prioritizes a limited number of high-impact research and analytics use cases. Collaborates with key partners and investigators to gather feedback, secure support, and make regular adjustments.

10. Identifies research opportunities and independently develops and leads data science and outcomes research projects from concept through dissemination, including research question development, study design, data identification, analysis, interpretation, and communication of findings.

11. Applies research and data science expertise and shares success stories and lessons learned with the Surgery Research Enterprise and broader research community. Teaches or coaches professionals in advanced analytics, data science, problem-solving methodologies, and related techniques to support professional development.

12. Monitors industry, healthcare, surgical research, and data science trends and best practices. Identifies opportunities to apply emerging methods to new research questions.

Other information:

Technical Expertise

  1. Strong organizational and problem-solving skills required, with an emphasis on attention to detail.
  2. Excellent written and oral communication skills, along with good interpersonal skills.
  3. Professional interaction with a diverse group of staff and users.
  4. Experience working independently and collaboratively with investigators and research teams to develop and execute research projects.
  5. Experience working with complex healthcare, clinical, research, or administrative datasets.
  6. Expert-level skills in research, data science, clinical and/or research decision-making processes, techniques, and tools (e.g., Snowflake, databricks, SAS, R, Python, SQL, etc.).
  7. Experience applying statistical techniques, machine learning, and advanced analytical methods to healthcare or clinical research data required.
  8. Demonstrated experience developing research questions, working with complex datasets, conducting advanced analyses, interpreting findings, and contributing to abstracts, presentations, manuscripts, or other scholarly products preferred.

Education and Experience

1. Education: Master's degree in data science, statistics, biostatistics, computer science, biomedical informatics, epidemiology, engineering, or a related quantitative field required. PhD or other relevant doctoral degree preferred.

2. Licensure: NA

3. Certification: NA

4. Years of relevant experience: Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience in data science, healthcare analytics, clinical research, outcomes research, or a related field required. Experience independently developing and leading research or analytical projects strongly preferred.

5. Years of supervisory experience: Preferred but not required.

Full Time

FTE: 1.000000

Description Pricing is one of the most consequential decisions Amazon makes — and the science behind it needs to be causally rigorous, not just predictive. The P2 Optimization Science (P2OS) team builds the machine learning systems that power Amazon's pricing decisions at scale: demand lift models, customer lifetime value frameworks, and the experimentation infrastructure that validates whether our pricing changes actually work. We're hiring an Applied Scientist to own causal inference at the intersection of ML and pricing experimentation. This role exists because our team has identified a real gap: the methodological bridge between econometric analysis (owned by our economists) and production-scale ML pipelines (owned by our engineers) needs a practitioner who lives in both worlds. You'll build CATE estimation models, design analysis workflows for pricing weblabs, and develop the reusable causal ML infrastructure that the broader team — including non-ML scientists — can rely on. This is not a research role. The bias here is toward shipping production-quality causal pipelines with real downstream business impact. You'll measure success by what changes in LTV estimates, what pricing errors your models help avoid, and whether the economists on your team can actually use what you build. If you're a scientist who wants to work on hard causal identification problems in a high-stakes production environment — and who finds satisfaction in making rigorous methods accessible to a broader team — this role is for you. Basic Qualifications - PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience - Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language - Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing Preferred Qualifications - Experience using Unix/Linux - Experience in professional software development Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. full_description:
Outset invented a better way to do research: AI-powered user interviews.

Global brands like Hubspot, Microsoft, Uber and Nestle use Outset to achieve deeper, qualitative insights about their users at unprecedented speed and scale.

The research industry is massive (>$140B and growing) and ripe for disruption. Incumbents are outdated, slow, and burdened by high-cost services. That's our opportunity.


Outset is backed by top Silicon Valley investors and raised a $30M Series B in December 2025—less than six months after our Series A—led by Radical Ventures with participation from M12 (Microsoft’s venture arm), 8VC, Y Combinator, and Adverb Ventures.

The raise follows a breakout year, with our business growing 8x as enterprise customers across industries adopt our category, AI‑moderated research, as the new standard for understanding people.

We’re a tight-knit team serving some of the world’s largest enterprises.

Outset builds digital twins: AI systems that represent specific real people and respond to research questions the way those people would. The Digital Twins Team runs an ongoing research program to measure and improve how faithfully these systems reproduce human responses and behavior, across a range of cross-sectional levels of analysis.

The Research Scientist works directly with and reports to the Head Scientist. Together you will choose what to study, design the studies, define how results are measured, interpret the findings, and write them up for internal decision-making and, where appropriate, for academic publication. You will bring current methodological training in computational social science, data science, survey-methodology, human-computation interaction, and experiment design.

Responsibilities

  • Co-design and run studies that compare system-generated responses with responses from humans, using both qualitative and quantitative measures.

  • Design, justify, and hone measures of performance.

  • Apply and adapt state-of-the-art statistical techniques common to survey methodology and large-scale social data analysis, to benchmark and improve sample- and population-level simulation performance.

  • Design evaluations and experiments with pre-specified analysis plans.

  • Design and oversee human rating studies, including rater training, coding rubrics, and inter-rater agreement measurement.

  • Design data collection from third-party data sources and directly from human participants, including longitudinal and repeated-measures studies.

  • Contribute to the research agenda for new modeling approaches, including evaluation of fine-tuned models and of model calibration.

  • Specify analyses precisely enough for an engineer to implement.

  • Co-author papers, preprints, and presentations.

Qualifications

  • A completed or nearly completed PhD in computational social science, communication, HCI, sociology, political science, psychology, statistics, or a related field.

  • Peer-reviewed publications on which you were a primary author.

  • Working command of graduate-level statistical methodology common to social science, including the assumptions behind each.

  • Experience analyzing large-scale telemetry and behavioral datasets, with attention to the validity of the resulting inference.

  • Familiarity with machine learning, spanning classical, nonparametric, and LLM-based approaches, including how transformer-based language models work, what fine-tuning does, and how the major model families differ.

  • Fundamentals of computing: file systems, software libraries, databases, SQL, and tabular data.

  • Ability to work in an environment where most code is produced through agentic coding tools, and to read and check that code.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience fine-tuning open-weight language models on survey, experimental, or behavioral data.

  • Experience building or evaluating calibrated confidence or error-prediction models, including deriving decision thresholds from human judgments.

  • Experience measuring similarity of open-ended text, for example with embedding-based methods.

  • Experience designing or running panel-based data collection with human participants.

  • Experience presenting research at academic and/or industry conferences.

  • Prior work on generative agents, digital twins, or simulation of human respondents.

  • Familiarity with the startup ecosystem

  • Familiarity with qualitative interviews and ethnographic methods

  • Familiarity with topics in computational linguistics
